Belgaum.x: Belgaum or Belgaon, officially Belagavi, is a city in Northwestern Karnataka, neighbouring to the state of Goa and Maharashtra, deeply embroiled in claims over this district. The winter capital of Karnataka, Belgaum is a city with a special history; often nicknamed "Kundanagari" which takes the name of a popular sweet made in Belgaum. There is a large minority with links to Goa and Maharashtra.

Goregaon (Raigad).x: Goregaon is a city in the Raigad district of Maharashtra near the river Kal.

Ichalkaranji.x: Ichalkaranji is a city in the Kolhapur district of South Maharashtra, India, known for its prominent textile and engineering industries. Often referred to as the “Manchester of Maharashtra,” the city is one of the country’s leading centres for grey fabric production and hosts a dense network of power looms, processing units, and garment manufacturers. Ichalkaranji has experienced rapid industrial growth since the mid‑20th century, evolving from a small princely town into a major economic hub with strong cooperative and entrepreneurial traditions.

sights.d: Ichalkaranji’s identity is deeply tied to its textile industry, and many visitors come specifically to observe the city’s power loom clusters and cooperative mills.
Dedicated to Lord Shiva, known for its peaceful atmosphere and traditional architecture.
Dedicated to Lord Dattatreya, an important spiritual centre for locals. The temple complex becomes especially lively during Datta Jayanti.
A local sports ground that hosts athletic events, kabaddi matches, and community gatherings.

Kanchipuram.x: Kanchipuram or Kancheepuram, formerly Conjeevaram, is a major pilgrimage site in northern Tamil Nadu. One of the most important spiritual centres of Hinduism, Kanchipuram has several medieval temples with spectacular architecture. It used to be the capital of the Pallava kingdom from the 4th to the 10th century, and was a centre of learning for all the major religions of South India.

sights.d: The highest, largest and most impressive temple in town, spanning 40 acres and dating back to the Pallava period.

Mahanandi.x: Mahanandi is a picturesque village surrounded by thick forests east of the Nallamala Hills near Nandyal, Kurnool District, Andhra Pradesh, India. Within 15 km of Mahanandi, there are nine Nandi shrines known as Nava Nandis. Mahanandi is one of the Nava Nandis.
